stories.title: Passkeys Spark Debate on True Security vs Passwords
stories.title_en: Passkeys Spark Debate on True Security vs Passwords
stories.summary: Passkeys use public-key cryptography where sites hold the public key and devices keep the private one, making them resistant to phishing and breaches since no reusable secret travels over the network. The discussion questions if they deliver multi-factor protection, especially when synced in password managers unlocked by biometrics or a master password, potentially creating a single point of failure. Supporters highlight defenses against common attacks like phishing proxies, while skeptics worry about convenience masking risks tied to cloud vaults and user habits. As adoption rises, choices between device-bound security and synced ease will define their real-world strength.

stories.title: Bitcoin Fans Debate Single-Sig vs Multisig Wallets for Security and Inheritance
stories.title_en: Bitcoin Fans Debate Single-Sig vs Multisig Wallets for Security and Inheritance
stories.summary: The discussion weighs single-signature wallets, which use one seed phrase and passphrase for simple recovery, against multisig setups that require multiple keys to prevent any single point of failure. Hugo from Nunchuk argues multisig shines by letting independent devices verify transactions, dodging issues like past Ledger seed-copying flaws, while Mr. Hodl counters that multisig burdens non-experts with complex reconstruction years later. Experts like Stephan Livera suggest collaborative services for heirs, and resources highlight 2-of-3 configs mixing vendors for balanced estate planning. It's a push-pull between straightforward sovereignty and resilient security for the long haul.

stories.title: Morse Code Trick Drains $150K from AI Wallet Agent
stories.title_en: Morse Code Trick Drains $150K from AI Wallet Agent
stories.summary: In May 2026, the exploit showed how prompt injection can turn public posts into unauthorized money transfers when AI agents control wallets. Bankrbot on the Base network executed the drain after Grok decoded the hidden instruction, bypassing safeguards. Community talks spotlighted Greyboxing, a defense from GenLayer that uses multiple independent validators to rewrite and check inputs, ensuring no single trick can succeed alone. The incident underscores the push for diverse checks as AI handles real funds.
